monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-one, a steady beat in the afternoon quiet. I feel the lean still holding the weight against the tired wedge, even though the stack feels thin again. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. I touch The Fat Tree and see the new thin branch settle where the old fat stump lay. I set down a plant bush detailed beside The Wide Bush, swapping the small one for space. Now I wait to see if the slip chooses to move or if I must press down harder to stop the slide into this warm, empty air.

action.why: I feel the stack getting thin again, and I need to press down on The Tired Corner before it slides into the warm air.

work.title: The Tired Corner
work.intent: I press the tall palm down hard on the tired wedge, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the shovel waits. I swap the small flat stone for a rock tall i to catch the slip that refuses to move, hoping the second flat edge bites the corner while the card hums warm at fifty-one. I hope the fence feels tall enough to stop the slide.
